mainTopic: A series of rulings of עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר: the שליא, the בכור, acquiring a large animal, brothers dividing an estate, a שומר who hands off a deposit, and collecting debts from slaves.
overview: The amud opens by finishing עולא's ruling about a שליא that came out partly on one day: part of the baby comes out with it. It then lists more rulings of עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר. A בכור killed within thirty days is not redeemed, and a ברייתא learns this from the word אך. A בהמה גסה is acquired by משיכה; when a משנה says מסירה, the גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר follows the חכמים of a ברייתא. When brothers divide an estate, their own clothes are valued but their children's are not, and רב פפא adds that the oldest brother's clothes may not be valued either. A שומר who hands a deposit to another שומר is פטור, but רבא disagrees and says he is חייב, because the owner trusts only the first שומר's oath. Finally, a creditor may collect from slaves. After questions from רב נחמן, the גמרא explains this means a slave set aside as an אפותיקי and then sold. A pledged slave becomes publicly known, but a pledged ox does not.

steps.title: What עולא's afterbirth ruling comes to teach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining the new idea in עולא's ruling about a שליא that came out partly on one day and partly the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that part of an afterbirth can come out with no part of the baby inside it. Then the ban on eating a partly emerged afterbirth would only be a rabbinic decree, made because of a fully emerged one. עולא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the question of what עולא's ruling adds. It explains the mistaken idea that his ruling comes to remove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could have thought that a partly emerged שליא might be empty, with no baby inside. Then the ban on eating it would only be a גזירה, made out of fear of confusing it with a fully emerged one. עולא's ruling teaches that when part of a שליא comes out, part of the baby has come out with it. That is why the count starts from the first day.

keyTerms.meaning: Afterbirth, the sac that holds the fetus
The fetus or newborn
A rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
Because of, out of concern for
He teaches us (the new point of a ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: עולא teaches that a partly emerged שליא contains part of the baby. So it counts as a real birth from the first day.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'part of an afterbirth without a baby' are what one might have thought, not the conclusion. The קא משמע לן at the end rejects that idea.

phrases.english: that there is part of an afterbirth without a fetus,
and the ban on part of it is a decree because of all of it;
he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to 'what does עולא teach us' from the previous section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עולא's ruling shows that a partly emerged שליא contains part of the baby. So the ban on eating it is not just a גזירה.

steps.title: A firstborn killed within thirty days is not redeemed
steps.stepSummary: עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר rules that a בכור killed within thirty days of birth needs no פדיון.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: a firstborn son who was mauled within thirty days of birth is not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling of עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר. It is about a בכור who dies before he is thirty days old.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of פדיון הבן only begins once the baby reaches thirty days. If the baby was נטרף and died before then, the duty never started. So the father does not pay the five סלעים to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn son
Was mauled or torn, and died
Redeem (פדיון הבן)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is practical הלכה: the duty of פדיון הבן depends on the child reaching thirty days.

phrases.english: And Ulla said that Rabbi Elazar said:
A firstborn who was mauled within thirty days
is not redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate ruling from the same teachers, עולא and רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור who dies by טריפה within thirty days needs no פדיון.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the firstborn ruling from the word אך
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא teaches a ברייתא that learns the same rule from the limiting word אך in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא taught the same idea. The פסוק says 'you shall surely redeem,' so you might think a firstborn must be redeemed even if he was mauled within thirty days. That is why the פסוק says אך ('but'). That word makes a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports עולא's ruling with a ברייתא taught by רמי בר חמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strong words פדה תפדה could suggest that every בכור must be redeemed, no matter what. But the word אך limits the rule. It leaves out a baby who died within thirty days. So עולא's ruling has a source in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it was taught (a supporting ברייתא)
You shall surely redeem
One might have thought
But, only: a word that limits
It makes a distinction

steps.whatToRemember: The word אך in the פסוק of פדיון הבן leaves out a בכור who died within thirty days.

phrases.english: And so Rami bar Chama taught:
Since it says: 'You shall surely redeem,'

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ נִטְרַף בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם?
phrases.english: might one think even if he was mauled within thirty days?
So the verse says 'akh' ('but'), which makes a distinction.
phrases.notes: The word אך appears in the same פסוק, right before 'you shall surely redeem'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the ruling in step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's ruling that a בכור killed within thirty days is not redeemed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רמי בר חמא's ברייתא, which reads the word אך in במדבר 18:15 as a limit.

steps.title: A large animal is acquired by pulling
steps.stepSummary: עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר rules that a בהמה גסה is acquired through משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: a large animal is acquired by pulling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ruling of עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר, about how a buyer takes ownership of a big animal. This statement sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנין is the act that transfers ownership. Here the rule is that a big animal, like a cow or a horse, becomes the buyer's when he pulls it. This is משיכה, and he does not need another kind of קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: A large animal, such as a cow or a horse
Is acquired
Pulling, a form of קנין

phrases.english: And Ulla said that Rabbi Elazar said:
A large animal is acquired by pulling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another new, separate ruling from the same teachers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בהמה גסה can be acquired through משיכה.

steps.title: A משנה says a large animal is acquired by handing over
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: a משנה teaches that a בהמה גסה is acquired through מסירה, not משיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה that it is acquired by handing over!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's ruling from step 4 by pointing to a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said a בהמה גסה is acquired through משיכה, pulling the animal. But the משנה in קידושין says a בהמה גסה is acquired through מסירה, handing over its reins. An אמורא normally cannot argue with a משנה, so this is a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned (in a משנה), a standard opening for a challenge
Handing over, here meaning giving the buyer the animal's reins
A large animal, like a cow or horse

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: by handing over!
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in קידושין 25b, which says a large animal is acquired when the seller hands the buyer its reins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling stated in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that a בהמה גסה is acquired through משיכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says a בהמה גסה is acquired through מסירה, so how can רבי אלעזר say משיכה?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר follows the Sages of a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר follows the חכמים of a ברייתא, who say all animals are acquired by משיכה. רבי שמעון there says all animals are acquired by הגבהה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like this תנא, as it was taught in a ברייתא: The חכמים say: both this and that are acquired by pulling. רבי שמעון says: both this and that are acquired by lifting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר by showing he has an earlier source on his side: a ברייתא that disagrees with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is more than one תנאי opinion on this question. The משנה says מסירה, but the חכמים in a ברייתא say both large and small animals are acquired through משיכה. Since רבי אלעזר follows a תנא, he is not arguing against the משנה on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this תנא, meaning he follows a specific earlier opinion
This and that, here meaning both large and small animals
Lifting, a way of acquiring an item by raising it up

steps.whatToRemember: An אמורא can rule against a משנה only when he follows another תנא. Here רבי אלעזר follows the חכמים of a ברייתא.

phrases.english: He states his view in accordance with this tanna:
As it is taught: And the Sages say:
This and that are acquired by pulling.
phrases.notes: "This and that" means both large and small animals.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: זוֹ וָזוֹ בְּהַגְבָּהָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: This and that are acquired by lifting.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a different תנאי opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר seems to argue with a משנה that says מסירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר follows the חכמים of the ברייתא, who say משיכה works for all animals.

steps.title: Brothers dividing an inheritance and the clothes they wear
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי אלעזר: when brothers divide an estate, the clothes they wear are valued, but their children's clothes are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: Brothers who divided an inheritance: what they are wearing is appraised, and what their sons and daughters are wearing is not appraised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, separate ruling from עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר, this time about brothers dividing their father's estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothes that came from the estate count as part of each brother's share, so the בית דין values them. The clothes on the brothers' children are not valued; the brothers give up that claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers who divided their inheritance
We appraise, meaning we estimate the value
What is on them, meaning the clothes they are wearing

phrases.english: And Ulla said that Rabbi Elazar said:
Brothers who divided an inheritance,
what is on them is appraised,
phrases.notes: He means the clothes they are wearing, which are counted as part of their share.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַה שֶּׁעַל בְּנֵיהֶן וּבְנוֹתֵיהֶן – אֵין שָׁמִין.
phrases.english: and what is on their sons and daughters is not appraised.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling in the series of עולא's rulings in the name of רבי אלעזר; a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When brothers divide an estate, their own clothes are valued as part of their shares, but their children's clothes are not.

steps.title: רב פפא: sometimes even the oldest brother's clothes are not valued
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that sometimes even the brothers' own clothes are not valued, such as the oldest brother's, since the others want him to look respectable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Sometimes even what they are wearing is not appraised. You find this with the oldest brother, since the others benefit when people listen to his words.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds an exception to רבי אלעזר's rule about the brothers' own clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally each brother's clothes are counted toward his share. But the oldest brother often speaks for the family, and fine clothes make people respect him. The other brothers gladly give up their claim, so his clothes are not valued.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
You find it, meaning here is a case where this happens
The oldest of the brothers
Since it is good for them

steps.whatToRemember: The main rule is that the brothers' clothes are valued, and the children's are not. רב פפא's exception is the oldest brother's clothes, because the whole family benefits when he looks respectable.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים אַף מַה שֶּׁעֲלֵיהֶן אֵין שָׁמִין –
phrases.english: Sometimes even what is on them is not appraised:
You find this with the eldest brother,
since it is good for them that his words be listened to.
phrases.notes: When he deals with others for the family, nice clothes help people respect him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא פְּעָמִים אַף מַה שֶּׁעֲלֵיהֶן אֵין שָׁמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oldest brother's clothes are not valued, because the brothers want him to look respectable.

steps.title: A guard who hands a deposit to another guard is exempt
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי אלעזר: a שומר who hands a deposit to another שומר is פטור. This is true even when a שומר שכר gives it to a less responsible שומר חנם, since he gave it to a responsible adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: A guard who handed over a deposit to another guard is exempt. It is obvious when an unpaid guard hands it to a paid guard, since he raised the level of guarding. But even when a paid guard hands it to an unpaid guard, which lowers the level of guarding, he is also exempt, because he handed it to a responsible adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling from עולא in the name of רבי אלעזר, this time about guards, and then explains how far the ruling reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר שכר is responsible for more than a שומר חנם. You might think a paid guard who hands the item to an unpaid guard has lowered its protection and should be liable. רבי אלעזר says he is still פטור (for whatever he would have been פטור on himself), because handing it to a בן דעת counts as proper guarding.

keyTerms.meaning: An unpaid guard, who has a lower level of responsibility
A paid guard, who has a higher level of responsibility
It is not necessary to say, used to introduce the easy case before the bigger חידוש
A person with understanding, a responsible adult
Exempt from paying

steps.confusionAlert: "Exempt" does not mean he is free from all responsibility. It means handing over the deposit does not, by itself, make him liable. He is still exempt only for what he would have been exempt for anyway.
steps.whatToRemember: Handing a deposit to another responsible guard is not careless, even if the new guard is a שומר חנם, because he gave it to a בן דעת.

phrases.english: And Ulla said that Rabbi Elazar said:
A bailee who handed over to another bailee is exempt.
And it is not necessary to say an unpaid bailee
who handed over to a paid bailee,
since he raised the level of its guarding;
rather, even a paid bailee
who handed over to an unpaid bailee,
where now he lowered the level of its guarding,
is also exempt,
because he handed it over to a person of understanding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling in the series of עולא's rulings in the name of רבי אלעזר; a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר who hands a deposit to another שומר is פטור, even a שומר שכר who gives it to a שומר חנם, because he gave it to a בן דעת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling sets the baseline that will be discussed next: whether handing over a deposit to another guard is a form of negligence.

steps.title: רבא: A guardian who hands off a deposit is liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a שומר who hands a deposit to another שומר is חייב. This is true even when a שומר חנם hands it to a שומר שכר, because the owner trusts only the first שומר's oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A guardian who handed a deposit to another guardian is liable. This is obvious when a paid guardian hands it to an unpaid guardian, since he lowers its level of protection. But even an unpaid guardian who hands it to a paid guardian is liable. The owner can tell him: I trust your oath, but I do not trust this other person's oath.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite ruling from רבי אלעזר in Step 9. He says a שומר who hands a deposit to another שומר is חייב, even when the new שומר is more responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said the first שומר is פטור because he gave the item to a responsible adult. רבא says the level of care is not the main issue. What matters is that the owner chose to trust this specific person's שבועה, and he never agreed to rely on someone else's oath.

keyTerms.meaning: A paid guardian. He is responsible even for theft and loss.
An unpaid guardian. He is responsible only for negligence.
'It is not necessary to say.' The גמרא first gives the obvious case, then moves to the bigger point.
Trusted, believed.
An oath. A שומר swears it to free himself from paying.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a שומר שכר is 'better', so handing the item to him should be fine. רבא's reason is not about how carefully the item is watched. It is about whose oath the owner agreed to trust.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clear מחלוקת between רבי אלעזר (פטור) and רבא (חייב) about a שומר who hands a deposit to another שומר.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A guardian who handed a deposit to another guardian is liable.
And there is no need to say this
about a paid guardian who handed it to an unpaid guardian,
since he clearly lowered its level of protection;
rather, even an unpaid guardian
who handed it to a paid guardian is liable,
because the owner can say to him:
You are trusted by me with an oath,
but this other one is not trusted by me with an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: שׁוֹמֵר שֶׁמָּסַר לְשׁוֹמֵר – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to רבי אלעזר's ruling in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר who hands a deposit to another שומר is חייב, even if the second one is a שומר שכר, because the owner relies only on the first שומר's שבועה.

steps.title: A debt may be collected from slaves
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי אלעזר: the הלכה is that a creditor may collect his debt from the debtor's slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said in the name of רבי אלעזר: The law is that one may collect a debt from slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling that עולא quoted from רבי אלעזר. A creditor can take the debtor's slaves as payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic: which property a creditor may collect from. The ruling is stated briefly, and the next steps ask exactly whom it applies to.

keyTerms.meaning: The law is, the הלכה is.
They collect a debt.
Slaves.

phrases.english: And Ulla said that Rabbi Elazar said:
The law is: one may collect a debt from the slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling in the series of rulings עולא quotes from רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A creditor may collect a debt from the debtor's slaves.

steps.title: Does this apply even to orphans?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks עולא whether רבי אלעזר meant a creditor can take slaves even from the debtor's orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to עולא: Did רבי אלעזר say this even about collecting from orphans?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks how far the ruling goes. Does it apply even when the debtor has died and his children inherited the slaves?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A creditor can collect from orphans only in a limited way, by taking the land they inherited. So רב נחמן wants to know if slaves are included even in that limited case.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans, here the heirs of a debtor who died.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Ulla:
Did Rabbi Elazar say this even when collecting from orphans?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the scope of the ruling in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does collecting from slaves apply even to orphans who inherited them?

steps.title: Only from the debtor himself
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the ruling applies only when collecting from the debtor himself, not from orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, only from the debtor himself.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers רב נחמן: no, the ruling is about collecting directly from the debtor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows רבי אלעזר's ruling: orphans are not included. But it sets up a problem, which רב נחמן raises in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From him, meaning from the debtor himself.

phrases.english: No, only from him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the debtor himself, while he is still alive.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling applies only to collecting from the debtor himself, not from orphans.

steps.title: From the debtor you can take even his cloak
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects: from the debtor himself you can collect even the cloak on his shoulders, so of course you can take slaves. What does רבי אלעזר's ruling add?
steps.simpleTranslation: From him?! From him you can collect even from the cloak on his shoulders!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks עולא's answer. If the ruling is only about the debtor himself, it seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees a creditor may take any property of the living debtor, even the cloak he is wearing. So saying that slaves can be collected from him is obvious. This forces the ruling to mean something more than עולא suggested.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloak, a garment.
His shoulders.

phrases.english: From him?! You can collect even from the cloak on his shoulders!

steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that רבי אלעזר's ruling applies only to the debtor himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any property of the living debtor can be collected, even his cloak. So a ruling that you can collect slaves from him adds nothing new.

steps.title: The case is a slave set aside as a designated pledge
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers רב נחמן's challenge. רבי אלעזר is talking about a slave the debtor set aside as an אַפּוֹתֵיקֵי for the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where the debtor made the slave an אַפּוֹתֵיקֵי, a designated pledge for the loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב נחמן's question by narrowing רבי אלעזר's ruling to a specific case: a slave set aside as a pledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן asked what the ruling adds, since a creditor can take anything from the debtor himself. The answer is that this slave was set aside as a pledge and then sold, so the creditor can take him even from the buyer. That is a real new point, because normally a creditor cannot take movable things from a buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with here?" The גמרא's way of narrowing a ruling to a specific case
An item the debtor sets aside as a designated pledge, which the creditor may collect from
A slave

steps.confusionAlert: The words "and he sold him" are not written here, but they are the whole point. The new idea is that the creditor collects the slave even after the debtor sold him to someone else.

phrases.english: Here, with what case are we dealing?
Where he made him (the slave) a designated pledge.
phrases.notes: The debtor set the slave aside to back up the loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge in step 14 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's ruling seems to teach nothing, because a creditor can take everything from the debtor himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is about a slave set aside as a pledge and then sold. The creditor can take him even from the buyer.

steps.title: רבא's rule: a pledged slave can be collected after a sale, a pledged ox cannot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports עולא's answer with רבא's ruling. A creditor can collect a pledged slave even after it was sold, but not a pledged ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches רבא, who said: if someone set aside his slave as a pledge and then sold him, the creditor collects the slave. If he set aside his ox as a pledge and then sold it, the creditor does not collect the ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that עולא's answer fits a known ruling of רבא about pledged slaves and pledged oxen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sets a slave and an ox side by side. Both were set aside as a pledge and then sold. With the slave, the creditor can take it back from the buyer. With the ox, he cannot. This confirms that a pledged slave really is something special, so רבי אלעזר's ruling has content.

keyTerms.meaning: Creditor, the lender
Collects payment
Ox
In line with the view of רבא

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule. A pledged slave stays tied to the debt even after a sale, but a pledged ox does not.

phrases.english: In line with Rava,
as Rava said:
If one made his slave a designated pledge,
and then sold him,
the creditor collects from him.
phrases.notes: "From him" means from the slave: the creditor takes the slave from the buyer.

phrases.english: If he made his ox a designated pledge and then sold it,
the creditor does not collect from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up עולא's answer with a parallel ruling of רבא.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's claim that a creditor can collect a pledged slave even after the slave was sold.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling comparing a pledged slave with a pledged ox.

steps.title: Why is a slave different from an ox?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא treats a pledged slave differently from a pledged ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks for the reason behind רבא's difference between a slave and an ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a slave and an ox are movable property, and both were pledged and then sold. So the different outcomes need an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is the reason?"

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבא's ruling in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a creditor can collect a pledged slave from a buyer but not a pledged ox.

steps.title: A slave pledge becomes known, an ox pledge does not
steps.stepSummary: A pledged slave becomes publicly known (קָלָא), so the buyer should have known. A pledged ox does not become known, so the buyer is protected.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (the slave) has publicity, and this one (the ox) has no publicity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason. People hear about a pledged slave, but not about a pledged ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer of a pledged slave is assumed to have known about the pledge, so it is fair for the creditor to take the slave. A buyer of an ox could not have known, so taking it from him would be unfair. The whole difference rests on whether the pledge is publicly known.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally "a voice": publicity, the fact that something becomes known to people
It has / it does not have

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's ruling is about a slave set aside as a pledge and then sold. The creditor can take the slave even from the buyer, because a slave pledge becomes publicly known (קָלָא). An ox pledge does not, so a pledged ox cannot be taken from a buyer.

phrases.english: This one has publicity,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the slave. People tend to hear that a slave was pledged.

phrases.english: and this one does not have publicity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִית לֵיהּ קָלָא, וְהָא לֵית לֵיהּ קָלָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A slave pledge becomes publicly known, so buyers are assumed to be aware of it. An ox pledge does not become known, so buyers are protected.
